## Krea 2 Turbo — 4-step distillation LoRA

Krea 2 Turbo normally needs **8 steps**. With this LoRA it runs at **4**.

### Files
| file | put it in |
| --- | --- |
| `krea2_turbo_bf16.safetensors` | `models/diffusion_models/` |
| `qwen3vl_4b_bf16.safetensors` | `models/text_encoders/` |
| `qwen_image_vae.safetensors` | `models/vae/` |
| `krea2_turbo_4step_rank_64_lora_comfyui.safetensors` | `models/loras/` |

The first three are from [Comfy-Org/Krea-2](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/Krea-2).

**The LoRA is independent of the base build.** It is applied on top of the diffusion model by ComfyUI's own loader, which handles any dequantisation, so a quantised or otherwise optimised build of Krea 2 Turbo behaves just as bf16 does. Please use whichever variant suits your hardware — set it in **Load Diffusion Model** and leave the rest of the workflow untouched.

This workflow ships **full bf16** only because it is the one build guaranteed to run everywhere: bf16 needs no backend-specific kernel, so it works on CUDA, Apple Silicon and CPU alike. Smaller options: `krea2_turbo_int8_convrot` (13.5 GB, either platform), or `krea2_turbo_fp8_scaled` (13.1 GB) which is **NVIDIA-only** — MPS has no `Float8_e4m3fn` support and fails at the sampler. The text encoder has bf16 and fp8 builds only; there is no int8 one.

> **Do not use `fp8_scaled` on Apple Silicon.** MPS has no `Float8_e4m3fn` support, so it fails at the sampler with *"Trying to convert Float8_e4m3fn to the MPS backend"*. It is fine on NVIDIA. `krea2_turbo_bf16` (26.3 GB) also works everywhere if you prefer full precision — just set the matching name in the loader.

### Settings that matter
- **steps 4**, **cfg 1.0** (Turbo is CFG-free), sampler **euler**, scheduler **simple**
- LoRA strength **1.0**
- The negative is a `ConditioningZeroOut` — at cfg 1.0 it is not evaluated, so there is nothing to write in it

Set steps back to 8 and bypass the LoRA node (Ctrl+B) to compare against stock Turbo.

### Metadata
The LoRA file carries its training details in its safetensors metadata: base model, method, sample count and the inference settings above.
